why: phase-426 W3 -- the node FQNs this executor publishes ROS parameter services under. ROS 2 needs no correspondent: a node there owns its own six services, so "which nodes have parameter services" is answered by the node you are holding. Ours registers a set per node onto ONE executor (RFC-0089's node model), so the list is a property of the executor and there is nothing else to ask. It exists to be ASSERTED: the six servers are created from exactly this list, so a host test can check what `ros2 param list` will enumerate without a wire, which is how W3's acceptance is met before W6's interop cell exists. Read-only and allocation-free (a `heapless::Vec` bounded by the executor's own node table), so it is safe to call from an embedded image's boot report.
